extensions.name: voice-narration
extensions.gives: Measured voice-overs from an approved script: one WAV per line from VoxCPM2 or Voicebox on the user's own computer, or from ElevenLabs through the app's connector, with a per-project pronunciation lexicon, a measurement of every take against its scene's limit, a consented speed-up of at most 5% and narration.lock.json (engine, model, voice source and consent, text sent, duration, verdict, SHA-256) for the mix.
extensions.studio_uses: Through the separate voice-narration plugin from this repository (skill voice-narration:narrate), the generation and measurement route for the voice-over lines Copy Voice approved: Audio Production Director's local voice engines guide hands off to it once the engine is chosen, and its WAV files and lock file go to FrameCut's timeline or Motion Graphics Workflow's sound step. Studio keeps the brief, copy locks, voice direction and final review.
extensions.not_for: Writing or shortening the script (Copy Voice), music or sound effects (Earshot, Audio Production Director), lip sync, or cloning a voice without its owner's recorded consent. Local engines are for the user's own computer: in a cloud session or a phone app installing them is advised against (several GB on a temporary disk, usually no GPU); use ElevenLabs through the connector or the script handoff there.

requires.note: Python 3.10+ with venv for the launcher and the VoxCPM2 environment
Optional: FFmpeg for the bounded speed-up and for converting non-WAV audio
PyPI and download.pytorch.org at the VoxCPM2 install, about 5 GB of weights once from huggingface.co; Voicebox runs locally on 127.0.0.1:17493; ElevenLabs only through the host's connector

extensions.rights: Apache-2.0 (FrameCore Works). No engine code or model is included: VoxCPM2 code and weights Apache-2.0 (OpenBMB), Voicebox MIT (each engine inside has its own licence), ElevenLabs under the user's own account and terms. A cloned voice needs its owner's recorded consent, kept in the lock file.

extensions.gives: The reviewed catalog of the tools FrameCore Works recommends (plugins and skills installable from its marketplace, plus app notes for desktop apps), each pinned with host-specific install notes, and Earshot built in: local measurement of a soundtrack against the picture, sound effects on cue frames from a bank of 252 code-made sounds, and, on the full tier, recognising, ranking and choosing sounds by listening.
